Create near-miss (mutant) copies of a JSON Patch library and CLI, plus a runner script. Project root /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f. Read /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch.mjs and /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/jsonpatch-cli.mjs (and the spec /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/.team/notes/jsonpatch-spec.md for context). NEVER modify the two originals; do not touch .team/scratch/ or test/. Other people are writing test/ in parallel; do not run the tests.

Each copy goes ONLY in /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/.team/near-miss/ named `<n>-jsonpatch.mjs` or `<n>-jsonpatch-cli.mjs` (n = 01, 02, ...), is a full copy of the original with exactly ONE plausible bug, and its first line is the comment `// near-miss: <the one bug>`. For CLI copies, drop the `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang line (a shebang on line 2 is a syntax error) and keep `import ... from './jsonpatch.mjs'` unchanged (the copy is swapped into the root to run). After creating each copy run `node --check` on it.

Library bugs (one per file):
01 INDEX_RE allows leading zeros: /^[0-9]+$/
02 `index <= arr.length` instead of `<` for non-add lookups (i.e. in arrayIndex ignore allowEnd: `index <= arr.length`)
03 jsonEqual uses Object.is(x, y) for primitives (0 and -0 unequal)
04 setMember uses plain assignment `obj[name] = value` (breaks __proto__)
05 child() uses `token in value` instead of Object.hasOwn
06 parsePointer decodes in wrong order: `.replace(/~0/g,'~').replace(/~1/g,'/')`
07 form check interleaved with apply (check and apply each op in one loop)
08 checkOperation reads op/path/from/value without hasOwn (`op.op`, inherited counts; e.g. `const name = op.op;` and `'value' in op`) — split into 08 (op via plain read `op.op`) and 09 (value presence via `'value' in op`)
10 checkOperation value presence via `Object.keys(op).includes('value')` (non-enumerable value missed)
11 move does add before remove (index counted before removal): insert then remove the original position, computing positions naively, e.g. `const value = walk(root, op.from, 'from not found'); add(root, op.path, value); remove(root, op.from, 'from not found');` — must be a plausible, working-for-objects implementation
12 move same-path special case removed (always remove then add)
13 copy without deepCopy (shares reference)
14 deepCopy via JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) (loses -0) — keep root primitive handling sane
15 isProperPrefix via string startsWith: `op.pathString.startsWith(op.fromString)` && different
16 form rule order swapped: 'missing value' checked before 'bad path'
17 '-' token on non-add lookup gives 'bad index' instead of notFound
18 hole skipped: form check uses patch.forEach (skips holes) — still must apply ops; e.g. `patch.forEach((p, i) => { ... })`
19 parsePointer accepts String objects: `if (typeof pointer !== 'string' && !(pointer instanceof String))` then `pointer = String(pointer)`
20 PatchError for non-array patch uses index undefined (`new PatchError('patch must be an array')`)
21 applyPatch with patch [] returns doc itself when no ops (`if (ops.length === 0) return doc;`)
22 jsonEqual treats arrays as objects (drop the Array.isArray branch so [] equals {})
23 jsonEqual compares only x's keys (no length check) so {a:1} equals {a:1,b:2}
24 'not an object' rule accepts functions (`typeof op !== 'object' && typeof op !== 'function'`)
25 add on existing member deletes then re-adds (`delete parent[last]` before setMember) — moves it last
26 remove on array uses `delete` semantics wrongly: `parent.splice(Number(last), 1)` replaced by `parent.length--`? no — instead use bad-index-less parsing: in arrayIndex use `Number(token)` validity `Number.isInteger(Number(token)) && token !== ''` instead of INDEX_RE (accepts 1.0, 1e0, ' 1')
27 parsePointer allows ~ followed by anything (regex check `/~$/` only)

CLI bugs (one per file):
31 size check skips the BOM (subtract 3 bytes from total when the data starts with EF BB BF) — implement it plausibly in collect
32 missing ENOTDIR mapping (only ENOENT -> no such file)
33 depth off-by-one: `depth + 1 >= limit`
34 BOM not stripped (TextDecoder with ignoreBOM: true)
35 all BOMs stripped: text.replace(/^﻿+/, '')
36 doc read in parallel with patch: `const [patch, doc] = await Promise.all([loadJson(patchArg), loadJson(docArg)]);`
37 both-stdin allowed: drop the `patchArg === STDIN && docArg === STDIN` usage check
38 output missing trailing newline
39 size uses fs stat size: before reading, if `(await handle.stat()).size > MAX_BYTES` throw too large, and the read loop no longer counts (collect without the limit for files) — stdin still counted
40 empty input treated as null: `value = text.trim() === '' ? null : JSON.parse(text)`
41 directory check missing: is-a-directory mapped to 'cannot read' (remove handle.stat directory check and EISDIR mapping)
42 depth check skipped for the patch input (only doc checked)
43 apply errors exit 1 instead of 4
44 3 arguments accepted (ignore extras: `args.length > 3`)

Also write /root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/.team/near-miss/run-near-miss.mjs (Node ESM, built-ins only, small functions, no console.log — write results with process.stdout.write): 
- ROOT = two dirs up from the script. Records sha256 of ROOT/jsonpatch.mjs and ROOT/jsonpatch-cli.mjs and copies both to a backup dir from fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()+'/jp-nm-').
- Optional argv filter: run only copies whose name starts with one of the given prefixes.
- For each `/^\d+-(jsonpatch(?:-cli)?\.mjs)$/` file in its dir (sorted): copy it over ROOT/<target>, run spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--test', 'test/'], {cwd: ROOT, encoding:'utf8', maxBuffer: 256MB, timeout: 300000}), and in a finally block restore the original from backup (always, also on failures). A near-miss is KILLED if exit status !== 0, SURVIVED if status === 0. Print one line per copy: `KILLED|SURVIVED <file> — <first-line comment> (fail N)` where N is parsed from the `# fail N` summary line.
- Install process.on('SIGINT'/'SIGTERM') handlers that restore originals and exit.
- At the end, verify sha256 of both originals equals the recorded value (print `originals intact` or exit 2 with a message), print `survivors: <count>`, exit 1 if any survived else 0.
Run `node --check` on the runner. Don't run it. Report the list of files created.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

content.text:
I couldn't create the mutant copies or run `node --check` on anything, so none of the work is done. The permission system denied my Bash call. It was a single command that would have made `.team/near-miss/`, run a generator script that writes all 40 copies, and run `node --check` on each. Nothing was written, and the two originals are untouched.

I didn't try to get around the denial. Writing about 40 files of roughly 210 lines each with the Write tool would not let me run `node --check`. It would also be easy to get wrong, so I stopped.

The plan was to put the generator in `/tmp/nm-gen/gen.mjs`, outside the project. It would take each of the 40 bugs and apply its exact-string edit to a copy of the original. It would fail if any edit didn't match exactly once. It would add the `// near-miss: <bug>` first line and drop the shebang from the CLI copies. After that I'd have written `run-near-miss.mjs` with Write and checked it with `node --check`.

To continue, either allow Bash for `mkdir`, `node` and `node --check` under `/root/bench-runs/h6-9b05e95f/.team/near-miss` and `/tmp/nm-gen`, or tell me to hand-write the files with Write and skip the syntax check. The first is much safer. Tell me which and I'll redo it.

Files created: none.

Tests run: none, as instructed.

One thing in the spec I'd read a certain way:
- **Mutant 22:** it needs `[]` to equal `{}`. Dropping only the `Array.isArray` branch would make any two arrays unequal, because `isObject` excludes arrays. So I'd swap in a local "is object-like" check that accepts arrays.
